audit.recode_to: undetermined (non-phonemic stress, placement variable/conditioning unknown; initial tendency in nouns and particles only) — or, if a position must be kept, fixed-dominant initial with not in the strict set and word-class restriction (nouns/particles), never fixed-strict
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote check passes: the Parks 1976 p.17 accent passage is verbatim in the Rosetta scan we hold. But the classification 'fixed-strict' (initial, counts as exceptionless (the strict set), word domain) is not what the held sources say. (a) Parks 1976, the deciding quote itself: stress 'does not seem to be phonemic'; in polysyllabic nouns and particles it 'generally, though not always' falls on the first syllable; in verbs placement is 'more variable' and its conditioning 'is not known' — in a polysynthetic language where verb forms dominate, this supports at most an initial tendency restricted to nouns/particles. StressTyp2 itself coded the pattern with msdomain=nouns and the editor note 'maybe verbs too?'. (b) Parks & Pratt 2008 p.15 (held page image, same author, 32 years later, Skiri dialect): stress not phonemic; recurring tendencies are initial OR peninitial (when V1 short and V2 long) AND antepenult or penult, 'but

sources.quote: No phonology, prosody or instrumental work on Pawnee is listed; descriptive items are Parks 1972/1976 grammar, Parks & Pratt 2008 dictionary (grammar_sketch), Parks 2001 'The Caddoan languages' HNAI 13:80-93 (overview), Hayden 1868, Cruickshanks 2011 MA (Sydney, complementation).
